simple.meaning: מַעֲדָן (maʻădân) is a Hebrew word meaning “a delicacy or (abstractly) pleasure (adverbially, cheerfully).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַעֲדָן (H4574) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 49:20, with occurrences in Genesis, 1 Samuel, Proverbs, Lamentations.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַעֲדָן (H4574) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַעֲדָן (H4574) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַעֲדָן (maʻădân) / H4574 is traced through Genesis 49:20, 1 Samuel 15:32, Proverbs 29:17, Lamentations 4:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H4574. maadan or maadannah [ מַעֲדָן ] noun [masculine] dainty (food), delight only plural; — מֶלָךְ מַעֲדַגֵּי Gen 49:20 royal dainties ; לְמַעֲדַנִּים הָאֹכְלִים Lam 4:5 those who ate (according to dainties) daintily ; more Generally לְנַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ מַעֲדַנִּים וְיִתֵּן Prov 29:17 he shall give delight to thy soul (|| וִינִידֶ֑ךָ ). — מַעֲדַנּוֺת , also below ענד . II. עדן (√ of following; compare perhaps Assyrian edinu , plain (in word-lists), Schr Cot Gen 2:8 , Dl Pa 79 f. ; other views see Di 2:8 ).
